clue.text: Sharp-pointed sticks and old-fashioned confinement to go after penal reform

indicators.note: this phrase places the confinement piece behind the rearranged letters
to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of penal are rearranged

parts.note: the stocks were a wooden frame used in former times to confine petty offenders

explanation.surface: A prison reformer brings in pointed sticks along with an antique pillory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' is the anagram signal, and 'to go after' places the old pillory last; 'penal' reads as a describing word but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine climbers' staffs tipped with iron spikes are exactly such sharp-pointed walking poles.

clue.text: Decoys the French deployed around the old city

indicators.note: the French article is spread out so that it wraps around the ancient city

parts.note: les is the French plural form of 'the'
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: French troops set out decoys around an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Baits that tempt animals or people into a trap are decoys.

clue.text: Cleric turns up in the school football team

indicators.note: the cleric piece goes inside the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman unexpectedly appears at a school football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the cleric's title, which sits 'in' the school. The answer is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: Eat and work to satisfy

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper or take food
to ply is to work steadily at a trade

explanation.surface: Eating and working are what keep a person content.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide what is needed is to satisfy a demand.

clue.text: Convenient exit provided by raised screen at back of duck coop

indicators.note: the screen piece is placed behind the other two pieces

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O
a pen is an enclosure such as a coop

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rood screen separates the nave from the chancel in a church

explanation.surface: A hen coop has a lifting screen at the back to let the duck out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses the church screen, and 'at back of' puts it after the duck and coop pieces; 'duck' looks like the bird but is a cricket zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlocked, unobstructed doorway offers a ready way out, figuratively free access.

clue.text: Worked with the hands as required by speaker

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: needed means required

explanation.surface: Dough was handled exactly as the presenter instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is pressed and folded manually when it is kneaded.

clue.text: Ruined bastion harbours the unsubmissive

annotationWithheld.why: Ruined bastion harbours the unsubmissive (13): the answer is an anagram of RUINED + BASTION, so 'Ruined' must be both fodder and the only anagram indicator; no separate indicator found

clue.text: Drunk but game

definitions.meaning: a board game played with round counters on a chequered board

explanation.definitionFit: Draughts are both swallows of drink and the British name for checkers.

clue.text: Tours even made offputting for the most daring

indicators.note: putting off can mean shifting things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, along with made

explanation.surface: Trips that are deliberately unpleasant for the boldest travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is TOURS EVEN MADE: 'offputting' is the anagram signal and 'made' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bold and willing to take risks is being daring.

clue.text: Scandinavian has choice of directions

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction
or is the word that offers a choice
SE is south-east, another compass direction

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian traveller is torn between which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice of directions' reads as N or SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse were the medieval people of Scandinavia, and the word describes them.

clue.text: Had rather be promoted

definitions.meaning: to have ... something is to have liked it better
an old sense of being advanced to higher office

explanation.surface: Someone would rather get promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means liked better and also advanced in rank, as in preferment.

clue.text: Restless, not having been paid

definitions.meaning: a bill that remains outstanding has not been settled

explanation.surface: Someone is fidgety because their wages have not arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means disturbed and agitated, and also of an account, outstanding and unpaid.

clue.text: Fruit fool is about right

indicators.note: the fool piece goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a dupe is a person easily fooled

explanation.surface: A fruit dessert, a fool, is nearly the correct thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts R inside DUPE. A fool is also a British fruit-and-cream dessert, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone fruit such as a plum or cherry is a drupe.

clue.text: Italian family getting nothing right, is in trouble

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of is in are stirred up

explanation.surface: A noble Italian house gets nothing right and lands in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IS IN into SINI after O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orsini were a powerful Roman noble dynasty of the Middle Ages and Renaissance.

clue.text: Makes damaging statement — river-man has pinched a pound!

indicators.note: to pinch is to steal, so the man takes the pound inside himself

parts.note: Sanders of the River is Edgar Wallace's colonial administrator hero
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a riverside man of having stolen a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has pinched' puts L inside SANDERS, the hero of the Edgar Wallace book Sanders of the River.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading false spoken claims that harm someone's reputation is what a defamer does.

clue.text: Songbird insisted, we hear, on talking

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed next to, so the talking piece follows
what we hear signals a word heard that is spelt differently

parts.note: 'would' can mean insisted, as in 'he would go, despite warnings'
chat means talking informally

explanation.surface: Someone insisted on talking about a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodchat shrike is a small perching bird of southern Europe.

clue.text: An undergarment I have found scratchy

annotationWithheld.why: An undergarment I have found scratchy (8): A + BRA + I'VE gives only ABRAIVE; the S of ABRASIVE has no source in the clue as held (perhaps 'undergarments' or 'undergarment's' was printed)
annotationWithheld.clue: An undergarment I have found scratchy

clue.text: Denunciation when assistance is withdrawn from large family

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: aid is assistance
a tribe is a large family group or clan

explanation.surface: Fierce criticism follows when a big family loses its benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter verbal attack is a denunciation.

clue.text: The artist took another nibble at this dish

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
re-bit means bit again

explanation.surface: A painter went back for a second bite of this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A rarebit is a British cheese-on-toast dish, Welsh rarebit.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: Someone who thinks he's an entertainer

parts.note: someone means a single person, hence the article a
a muser is one who ponders

explanation.surface: Someone fancies themselves as a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A MUSER, one who muses.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who amuses is someone who delights others.

clue.text: In it an animal turns up for a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An animal pops up in a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the whole run INITRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin and vermouth is a classic drink.

clue.text: Tap-dancing pigs circle square

indicators.note: the letters of pigs jig about into a new order

parts.note: O is circular in shape
a T-square is a draughtsman's instrument

explanation.surface: Pigs tap-dance around a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap-dancing' must be split: 'Tap' is the definition and 'dancing' rearranges PIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or tap on a cask.

clue.text: Fume, having rod in pickle

indicators.note: being in a pickle is being in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone fumes at being caught in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A nidor is a smell of cooking meat, a fume or vapour.

clue.text: It could be made up as a trap

definitions.text: It could be made up as a trap

indicators.note: these words suggest the following letters may be fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A device that could be assembled as a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be made' rearranges UP AS A TRAP; the whole clue also describes the answer, since equipment can be rigged as a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment or gear can be rigged up to work as a snare.

clue.text: Model, tall, displaying plenty of leg

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
high means tall

explanation.surface: A tall model shows off a lot of leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper part of the leg between hip and knee is its most substantial portion.

clue.text: Beating the endless thievery

indicators.note: endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: robbing is theft

explanation.surface: Thieves are being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes E off THE to leave TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulsing or pounding, like a heart, is beating.

clue.text: Enigmatic expression

parts.note: a turn of phrase whose meaning cannot be worked out from the words themselves

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase like 'kick the bucket' carries a meaning not deducible from its words, so it is enigmatic.

clue.text: Tree in road set on fire by this lamp

indicators.note: the tree goes inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
to light is to set on fire

explanation.surface: A tree in the road has been set ablaze by the nearby lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the tree inside the road abbreviation; the surface's lamp setting the tree alight is pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp on a post illuminating a road is this.
